item.title: Velvet's Mini Burlesque Variety Show — Fri Oct 16, 7:30 PM — 104 N. Main Street
item.description:
Sebastopol’s resident burlesque dancer Velvet Thorn is going to Japan this November! She needs your help to get to Kobe for the Japan International Burlesque Festival. What better way to raise some support for her travels than doing what she knows best: putting on a show! On October 16th at The Main Street Theater Sebastopol enjoy an evening of burlesque performances from artists across the Bay Area! There will also be a costume sale in the lobby and Velvet Thorn merch available. Velvet has been producing burlesque shows for over a year across SOCO. If you have enjoyed any productions from Epineux Productions or come to support her at another local show, or you are interested to see what burlesque is all about drop by for an evening of community fun! Lobby opens at 6:45pm, Theater opens at 7:00pm, and Show at 7:30pm
Source: Sebastopol Calendar

item.description:

Coffee cupping, or coffee tasting, is the practice of observing the tastes and aromas of brewed coffee. Join us to sample coffees from around the world side-by-side, develop your palate and discover coffees you LOVE that you never knew existed!

item.title: Saturday Harvest Market at Sonoma Garden Park — Sat Oct 17, 9:00 AM — Sonoma Garden Park
item.description:
Saturday Harvest Markets are back! 2026 Harvest Markets reopen March 21 and continue until December. Harvest Markets take place every Saturday, 9:00 am-1:00 pm. The Harvest Market is a great place to pick up organic produce, fresh flowers, and vegetable starts from our 6.1 acre sustainable garden! We also sell locally sourced olive oil, honey, and farm fresh eggs from our Sonoma neighbors. The market accepts credit cards and Apple Pay. Remember to bring your reusable shopping bag! Photo by Melania Mahoney

item.title: Saturday Drawing Club — Sat Oct 17, 12:00 PM — City Arts Gallery
item.description:
Solano County Arts Council invites you to hang out and draw. This is a weekly, free event, open to all!
After grabbing some fresh produce at the Farmer's Market around the corner, stop by to doodle and draw in a casual, fun, and supportive environment. All ages, all skill levels. Just a fun place to hang out, meet new people, and draw together!
Bring your own supplies if you can, limited supplies will be made available. Please no inks or paints. Children must be accompanied by parent or guardian.
The art gallery is open during drawing club and showcases local original art. The gallery is regularly open Thursdays, Fridays, and Saturdays from 10 am to 2 pm, except second Fridays when it's open from 5 pm to 9 pm for Vallejo Second Friday Artwalk. We hope you'll stop by!

item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Sun Oct 18, 8:00 AM — Marin County Civic Center
item.description:
Price: Free Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market. Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine. www.aginstitutemarin.org
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Reuse in Art, Reuse in Life: A Conversation Between Ali Gass and Phoebe Schenker — Sun Oct 18, 3:30 PM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Join Alison Gass, Founding Executive Director of the ICA San Francisco, and Phoebe Schenker, Executive Director of Reuse Alliance, for a wide-ranging conversation about reuse in contemporary and historical art and why it is more relevant than ever.
The discussion will explore the many ways artists have engaged with reuse, from incorporating found and reclaimed materials to making reuse itself a central subject of their work. Together, Gass and Schenker will consider how reuse connects to broader cultural conversations about creativity, sustainability, consumption, and value, while also exploring how reuse can become a creative practice in our own everyday lives.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

This class is for art explorers of all levels!
Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.
In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. After grabbing some fresh produce at the Farmer's Market around the corner, stop by to doodle and draw in a casual, fun, and supportive environment. All ages, all skill levels. Just a fun place to hang out, meet new people, and draw together!
Bring your own supplies if you can, limited supplies will be made available. Please no inks or paints. Children must be accompanied by parent or guardian.

item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Sun Oct 25, 8:00 AM — Marin County Civic Center
item.description:
Price: Free Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market. Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine. www.aginstitutemarin.org
Source: North Bay Bohemian
